record.body:
## Rationale

The commands are the smallest set that lets a clean repo go from claim text to a manifest that verdict accepts. Signing reuses the allowlist and ssh-keygen pattern of amendments under its own namespace, so a human witness cannot be replayed as an amendment or an attestation.

## Counter-argument

A sign verb would spare users the ssh-keygen call. It would also add an untested-by-spec surface; this phase leaves it for later.

payload.alternatives: hand-edit JSON then freeze only; a claim sign CLI verb in this phase; recording support hashes in a new manifest field
payload.choice:
aff claim add --cwd DIR --id ID --text TEXT --test NODE (repeatable) appends a claim with empty oracle_hashes to DIR/.affidavit/manifest.json, creating it when absent and refusing a duplicate id; aff freeze [--cwd DIR] [CLAIM...] sets each claim's oracle_hashes to sha256 of the working-tree file for every distinct path in its test node ids and refuses a missing file (support files are frozen by being listed in support_files; freeze requires each to exist); aff lint claims [--cwd DIR] prints '<claim-id>: compound claim' for text containing ' and ', ' as well as ', ';' or two or more sentences, and '<claim-id>: trust-scoped claim' for text naming agent-supplied input, exiting 1 on any finding; a claim with witness 'human' carries an ssh signature string over 'affidavit-claim v1
claim: <id>
text: <text>
' in namespace affidavit-claim, verified against .affidavit/allowed_signers at --at, with reasons 'human signature missing' and 'human signature invalid'
